4 اسمعهُ , inf. n. إِسْمَاعٌ: see 2, in four places. ―
-b2- He told him [a thing]. (Msb) ―
-b3- He made him to understand: the verb being used in this sense in the Kur [viii. 23], لَوْعَلِمَ ٱللّٰهُ فِيهِمْ خَيْرًا لَأَسْمَعَهُمْ [Had God known any good in them, He had made them to understand]. (TA.) ―
-b4- أَسْمَعَكَ ٱللّٰهُ May God not make thee to be deaf. (TA.) ―
-b5- أَسْمَعَتْ She sang. (TA.) One says to a female singer, أَسْمِعِينَا Sing thou to us: thus used in a verse of Tarafeh. (TA.) ―
-b6- أَسْمَعْتَ Thou hast said a saying that ought to be heard and followed. (Har p. 398.) ＝
-A2- اسمع الدَّلْوَ (tropical:) He made, or put, a مِسْمَع [q. v.] to the bucket. (S, K, TA.) And in like manner, اسمع الزِّنْبِيلَ (K) (tropical:) He made, or put, what are termed مِسْمَعَانِ to the basket. (TA.) ＝
-A3- أَسْمِعْ بِهِمْ وَأَبْصِرْ; and أَبْصِرْ بِهِ وَأَسْمِعْ; see art. بصر.
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
